title: Loops, std::array, and std::vector
summary: Traverse fixed and dynamic sequences with range-for and indexed loops while preserving bounds, iterator validity, and accumulator invariants.

Compile and test behavior with observable evidence

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: `std::array<T,N>` represents a fixed-size sequence and `std::vector<T>` owns a dynamically sized contiguous sequence. Prefer range-based `for` when only values matter and use a reference when mutation is intentional. `size()` returns an unsigned size type; use consistent index types. `at()` checks bounds and throws, while `operator[]` requires the caller to guarantee a valid index. Adding to a vector can invalidate iterators, pointers, and references, so do not grow it while traversing through those handles. Standard algorithms often express intent more clearly than manual loops.
